name: Camille Minaudo
statement: I study how lakes and rivers change colour, breathe and exchange carbon, from satellite pixels down to floating chambers.
bio: I'm a limnologist working at the interface of optical remote sensing and aquatic biogeochemistry. My current work combines satellite archives with high-frequency field measurements to understand how inland waters respond to warming, nutrient change and drought.

I trained in hydrology and water-quality modelling, did my PhD on the eutrophication of the Loire River, and later worked on Lake Geneva's primary production and optical properties at EPFL. I'm now based at the University of Barcelona, where I work across French, Spanish, Catalan and English.

themes.title: Optical remote sensing of inland waters
themes.text: Reading water colour from Sentinel-2, Landsat and ESA CCI Lakes to track water quality, whiting events and saline fronts at scales from one lake to thousands.

themes.title: Carbon and greenhouse-gas fluxes
themes.text: Measuring CO_2 and CH_4 exchange with floating chambers, separating ebullition from diffusion, and building open tools to process flux data reproducibly.

themes.title: Primary production and lake metabolism
themes.text: Estimating primary production, calcification and ecosystem metabolism from bio-optical models, high-frequency oxygen and ¹³C incubations.

themes.title: Rivers, catchments and water quality
themes.text: Linking nutrient export, hydrology and long-term trends across river networks at the global scale.
